clue.text: I work hard, putting party above monarch

parts.note: the Labour Party is one of Britain's main political parties
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: Someone who toils hard puts loyalty to their party ahead of the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'putting' one piece 'above' another stacks them top to bottom. Every clue in this puzzle begins with 'I', here the speaking worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual worker toiling at heavy tasks is a labourer, speaking here in the first person.

clue.text: I moved out of country for a length of time

indicators.note: if I has moved out of the country, that letter leaves the country's name

parts.note: Spain is a European country

explanation.surface: Someone emigrated from their homeland for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I moved out of country' reads as a personal memoir, but it means take the letter I out of SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is a stretch or period of time, as in a life span.

clue.text: I have medical men around of varying types

indicators.note: the doctors stand around, so their letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: DRS is the abbreviation for doctors
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A patient is attended by doctors of all kinds.
explanation.walkthrough: The contraction I've supplies three letters; 'around' says the doctors enclose them. Divers in this sense is old-fashioned, not the plural of diver.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers is an old adjective meaning several or sundry, of assorted kinds.

clue.text: I will fish around for scarf

indicators.note: fishing around something here means the fish's letters wrap around it

parts.note: the manta is a large ray, a fish
I will contracts to I'll

explanation.surface: A speaker plans to go fishing in search of a lost scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I will' becomes the contraction I'll, and 'around' has the fish wrap it. A manta is a giant ray.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantilla is a lace scarf worn over the head and shoulders, Spanish style.

clue.text: I concentrate power, as moderate protecting a Liberal

indicators.note: one piece protects another by surrounding it

parts.note: a centrist holds moderate political views

explanation.surface: A politician claims to gather power as a moderate who shields a Liberal colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' places A and L inside CENTRIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A centralist favours drawing political authority into a central government.

clue.text: I suffer from this in Indian city

definitions.meaning: read as '...', the ailment I personally suffer from
A city in Karnataka, southern India

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: split the name into two words, the sore that is mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysore, now officially Mysuru, is a well-known southern Indian city; split in two it says my sore.

clue.text: I, perhaps, reset precious stone

indicators.note: to reset is to set again in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jeweller wonders whether to remount a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reset' rearranges IPERHAPS; 'reset' looks like a jeweller's term for remounting the stone, which fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphire is a blue gemstone, a variety of corundum.

clue.text: I clued, anagrammatically, a mathematician

indicators.note: the clue openly says the letters before it are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver admits to having cracked a clue about a mathematician by rearranging it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anagrammatically' rearranges ICLUED.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was the ancient Greek mathematician famous for his geometry, the Elements.

clue.text: I repeatedly heard this nocturnal creature

indicators.note: repeatedly asks for the result twice in a row
heard tells us the word I is taken as spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like AYE

explanation.surface: Someone keeps hearing a night animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns I into its sound-alike AYE, and 'repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The aye-aye is a lemur of Madagascar that forages at night.

clue.text: I do without a bit of money

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the swindle wraps around the letter

parts.note: to do someone is to con or swindle them

explanation.surface: Someone manages to go without a little cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do without' looks like 'manage without', but 'without' means outside: CON goes around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin is a small piece of metal money.

clue.text: I got in awful tax notice, hence agitated state

indicators.note: the letter I gets in among the rearranged letters
awful suggests something badly mangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A taxpayer is upset after receiving a dreadful tax demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges TAXNOTICE, and 'got in' slips I in among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Excitation is a state of being stirred up or roused, here agitation.

clue.text: I, so to speak, can be affected by it and I'll be regularly seen in it

definitions.text: I, so to speak, can be affected by it and I'll be regularly seen in it

parts.words: I, so to speak, can be affected by it and I'll be regularly seen in it
parts.note: the letter I sounds like the organ of sight, which can suffer this inflammation; the word itself has the letter in every other position

explanation.walkthrough: Two cryptic hints: 'I, so to speak' is the eye, and the six-letter word shows the letter I at first, third and fifth places.
explanation.definitionFit: Iritis is inflammation of the iris, a condition affecting the eye.

clue.text: I sentenced improperly, showing such inclinations

indicators.note: improperly signals the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A judge confesses to passing wrong sentences, revealing his biases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improperly' rearranges ISENTENCED; 'showing such' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendencies are inclinations or leanings towards some behaviour.

clue.text: I will, with rich editor, become destined to fail

parts.note: I will contracts to I'll
fat means rich, as in fat profits

explanation.surface: Someone foresees their doom after teaming up with a wealthy editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-fated describes something doomed, bound by fate to come to grief.

clue.text: I tear into outlaw

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
to rend is to tear apart

explanation.surface: A speaker attacks a bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals a container. The definition is just 'I': the setter, who signs himself with this pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter of this puzzle uses this pseudonym, so the first person speaking is him.

clue.text: I am present, working on offer

parts.note: to be at something is to be working on it, as in 'at it' or 'at the job'
a tender is a formal offer

explanation.surface: Someone at an auction says they are here and bidding.
explanation.definitionFit: An attender is someone who turns up and is present at an event.

clue.text: I, for example, could be London landlord?

definitions.meaning: the clue's own opening is an upper-case ...
London is the national ..., and a landlord is one who lets property

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a playful split: someone who lets in the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: I is an upper-case character; jokingly, a landlord letting rooms in London lets in the capital.

clue.text: I put in names incorrectly for these flowers

indicators.note: the number is put inside the other word
incorrectly means the combined letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone mislabels flowers in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the Roman numeral one; 'put in' is the container and 'incorrectly' the anagram of the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Anemones are flowering plants of the buttercup family, windflowers.

clue.text: I set after Frenchman's name the Russian equivalent

indicators.note: set after places the letter after the name

parts.note: Andre is a common French first name

explanation.surface: A speaker places himself after a Frenchman's name to make its Russian form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set after' places I after ANDRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrei is the Russian form of the French name Andre, both meaning Andrew.

clue.text: I must go with green in fashion for English town

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the fashion word

parts.note: ton is an old word for high fashion
vert is green in French and in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone must go green and stylish to suit a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'ton' meaning fashion and 'vert' meaning green are crossword favourites. Tiverton is a market town in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiverton is a town in Devon in England.

clue.text: I painted Napoleon with some striking results

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An artist boasts of portraying Napoleon to dramatic effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks out the run INGRES from 'striking results'; 'with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres painted Napoleon I on his Imperial Throne.

clue.text: See 17
I serve a need extremely efficiently

parts.note: to lack is to need

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last, of the following word

explanation.surface: A servant boasts of meeting needs with great efficiency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the outer letters EY of 'efficiently'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lackey is a servant or footman, someone who waits on others.

clue.text: I note, after effort put into recent pieces, how these clues must appear!

indicators.note: after places I and the note at the end
the effort is put into the rearranged letters
to break recent into pieces is to rearrange its letters

parts.note: a go is an attempt or effort
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: The setter remarks that his clues must seem self-obsessed after all this work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' signals the anagram, 'put into' the container and 'after' that I and the note come last. Every clue in the puzzle starts with I, hence the self-centred look.
explanation.definitionFit: Clues all starting with the first person singular appear self-centred, obsessed with the self.

clue.text: I had love left for one greatly admired

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone had abandoned love for a hero they worshipped.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a person adored or venerated by fans.

clue.text: I may stand for it in part of church, say

indicators.note: say means the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: an aisle is a passage in a church

explanation.surface: Someone may be standing in the church aisle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives a word sounding like AISLE. I is the map abbreviation for an island, as in I of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: On maps the single letter I abbreviates island, as in I of Wight.

clue.text: I reportedly joined with leftist in night flight

parts.note: red means a left-winger

indicators.note: reportedly says the letter is taken as spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE

explanation.surface: Someone says they joined a left-wing companion on an overnight flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns I into EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-eye is an overnight flight, so called because passengers arrive bleary.

clue.text: I feel so awfully cold inside frozen blocks

indicators.note: inside puts the cold letter within the others
awfully suggests the words are badly mangled, so rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A speaker feels terribly chilly among blocks of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges FEELSO to EFLOES, and 'inside' puts C between I and those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice floes are sheets of floating ice, frozen slabs on the sea.
